question: How does a Kubernetes Secret store sensitive data according to the API schema — what fields does it define and how is data encoded?
selection_rationale: SO answer score 0. D1=3 D2=3 D3=3 D4=1 D5=2. G4 new coverage.

ground_truth.answer: Secret stores sensitive data in two fields: data (a map of string keys to base64-encoded byte strings — the standard storage field) and stringData (a map of string keys to plain string values — write-only convenience field, not returned by GET; takes precedence over data for the same key). The type field (string) categorizes the Secret (e.g. Opaque, kubernetes.io/tls, kubernetes.io/service-account-token). A Secret is namespaced — metadata.namespace scopes it to a single namespace.
context: io.k8s.api.core.v1.Secret: stores sensitive data; data maps string keys to base64-encoded byte values; stringData maps string keys to plain text (write-only, merged into data on persist)
